concept.name: Kubernetes
concept.title: Kubernetes, for Customer Success
concept.definition: Kubernetes is the platform customers use to run containerized applications: it deploys the app, keeps copies running, scales when traffic grows, and recovers when something breaks.
concept.problem: Customers need applications to stay available and scale without manually managing every machine.

nodes.label: Customer's App
nodes.caption: what they ship
nodes.description: The customer's product or workload. Kubernetes is the platform underneath it, not the application itself.

nodes.label: Users
nodes.caption: call the application
nodes.description: People or systems using the customer's product through a stable address.

nodes.label: Container
nodes.caption: the packaged app
nodes.description: A container packages the application so the same build can run consistently across environments.

nodes.label: Deploy
nodes.caption: release a version
nodes.description: Kubernetes places a released application version onto the cluster as running copies.

nodes.label: Stable Access
nodes.caption: Service — one address
nodes.description: A Kubernetes Service gives users one address while running copies change behind it.

nodes.label: Scale
nodes.caption: add or remove copies
nodes.description: Kubernetes can add copies for more traffic and remove them when demand falls.

nodes.label: Recover
nodes.caption: restart what breaks
nodes.description: Kubernetes replaces failed copies so a machine or process failure does not automatically become product downtime.

nodes.label: Running Copies
nodes.caption: the live application
nodes.description: These are the live application copies. Customers may call them Pods in architecture conversations.

groups.label: Kubernetes Cluster — deploy, scale, recover, manage
groups.description: The Kubernetes platform that runs and manages the customer's containerized application.

chapters.title: Where Kubernetes sits
chapters.explanation: The customer's application is packaged as a Container. Kubernetes is the platform that runs that package across machines.

chapters.title: Deploy the application
chapters.explanation: Deploy means releasing a version onto the cluster. Kubernetes places running copies of the packaged application.

chapters.title: Scale and recover
chapters.explanation: When traffic grows, Kubernetes adds copies. When a copy breaks, Kubernetes replaces it. This is the operational value customers usually mean.

chapters.title: How users reach the app
chapters.explanation: Users call one stable Service address. Kubernetes routes them to healthy running copies even while those copies are replaced.

roleRelevance.title: Why this matters for a Customer Success Manager
points: Follow customer architecture conversations when Kubernetes appears in the stack.
Connect deployment, scaling, and recovery to reliability outcomes customers care about.
Distinguish an application issue from capacity or platform recovery symptoms.
Use customer vocabulary accurately without needing scheduler internals.

contextCards.title: How the pieces fit
points: The application is packaged as a Container.
Kubernetes runs and manages copies of that Container.
A Service keeps access stable while copies change.

contextCards.title: Terms customers may use
points: Cluster means the whole Kubernetes environment.
A Node is one machine; a Pod is one scheduled running unit.
Deploy, scale, and recover are jobs the same platform performs.

contextCards.title: Why customers use it
points: Avoid managing every machine by hand.
Keep products available through individual failures.
Run the same packaged application across environments.
